promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Heat, short sleep and a work deadline stacked up on you, so we are not making up miles. We hold the shape of the week, dial the pieces back a touch, and get a modest marathon-pace block in.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: No, do not make up the miles. In that heat and on that sleep, chasing the lost 2 mi on Sunday and the 5 mi on Thursday would just deepen the hole. We rebuild instead: a slightly lighter easy day Tuesday, a shorter marathon-pace piece Wednesday rather than threshold, and a 12 mi long run on Sunday to put the long effort back in the legs cleanly.

new.analysis:
## What happened

You followed Monday, Tuesday, Saturday and the first chunk of the week well, and made two honest calls under heat: pulling the threshold after two reps and ending the long run at 11 mi. Thursday's easy run dropped out. On a normal week I would push back, but this week the ambient conditions and the 5.5 hr sleep made 27 mi plenty.

## Why the numbers look how they do

Easy heart rate climbed from 138 to 151 for roughly the same pace. That is heat, dehydration and sleep, not fitness lost. Hard minutes went up because Wednesday and Sunday both tipped into zone 4 as your heart worked harder to shed heat, which is also why easy time in zones 1 and 2 dropped to 10.8 percent. I am not alarmed by that share this week, given the conditions; I expect it to climb back toward 70 percent next week with the AC on.

## Why next week looks the way it does

You are 8 weeks out and still in the build, so I want to keep a quality session and a long run on the board, just at a size you can actually finish well. Wednesday swaps threshold for a shorter marathon-pace block at about 8:35/mi, which is your 3:45 pace: it is the specific work that matters now, and it costs less than threshold in recovery. Sunday rebuilds the long run to 12 mi before we push toward 14 – 16 the following weeks.

## What I need from you

If the apartment is cool again and you sleep over 7 hr most nights, this week will feel very different. If sleep stays under 6 hr or easy heart rate is still above 148 by Wednesday morning, drop the marathon-pace piece and run the whole thing easy; tell me and we will adjust.

safetyCallouts.title: Sleep and heat load.
safetyCallouts.body: Several nights under 5 hr with high stress is worth flagging to yourself. If you feel lightheaded, unusually breathless or your resting heart rate stays elevated after a cool night, see a clinician rather than training through it.
